title: Communications During Network Outages
summary: Phone battery conservation, alternative communication channels, and offline emergency plans.
content:
1. Smartphone Battery Discipline:
- Switch devices to 'Low Power Mode' / 'Battery Saver Mode'.
- Turn screen brightness down to minimum. Turn off Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, location services/GPS, and close background applications.
- Turn off redundant household phones. Keep one master phone switched on and preserve others as reserve units.

2. SMS Over Voice Calls:
- Send text messages (SMS) rather than placing voice calls. SMS requires significantly less network bandwidth and will automatically queue and send when signal pulses momentarily.

3. 999 Emergency Roaming:
- If your personal network shows 'No Service', dial 999 or 112. Mobile phones automatically switch to any working UK carrier (EE, Vodafone, O2, Three) to transmit emergency distress calls.

4. Digital Landline Warning:
- Modern digital fibre/VoIP landlines connected via broadband routers stop working during power cuts. Keep mobile devices or battery backups ready.

5. In-Car Device Charging:
- Charge phones using vehicle USB ports if available. Only run the engine in a well-ventilated outdoor open driveway or street. Never run a car inside an enclosed garage.

6. Battery or Wind-Up Radio:
- Keep an analogue FM/AM/DAB radio with spare batteries.
- Local news & alerts: BBC Radio London (94.9 FM - verify locally).
- National news & emergency broadcasts: BBC Radio 4 (92-95 FM / 198 LW).

7. Offline Coordination:
- Agree on a physical local meeting point with family in case networks collapse entirely.
- Keep written paper copies of essential phone numbers, medical notes, and family contacts.
